title: My Former Hopes Are Dead
description: My Former Hopes Are Dead in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 8, “The shining Light”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My for-mer hopes are dead, My ter-ror now be-gins; I feel, a-las! that I am dead In tres-pass-es and sins.

lines: I feel, alas! that I am dead
But sure, a friendly whisper says,
I see, or think I see,
A beam of day that shines for me,
I'll gaze upon it while I run,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
